speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been a long, hard slog, full of unexpected twists and turns, and I thank everyone for your cooperation, hard work and sacrifices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through our collective efforts, we have found our way through this pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Yesterday, we reached a new milestone and moved to Disease Outbreak Response System Condition (DORSCON) Green.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In parallel, industries that were hardest hit by COVID-19 are seeing continued recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Demand has picked up for sectors, like food and beverages (F&B) and retail.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Air travel has resumed and Singaporeans are travelling again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore Airlines flights are filling up, pilots and cabin crew are busy flying, and Changi Airport is buzzing with life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the start of 2022, we had anticipated tightness in energy markets and supply chain bottlenecks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the outbreak of the Ukraine war caught many by surprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite it happening halfway across the world, the war set off a chain reaction of shockwaves throughout the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Oil and gas prices shot up; we experienced a global shortage of grain and other food items.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some countries also imposed export bans to secure their own domestic needs, worsening global supply bottlenecks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Inflation was further fuelled by tight labour markets across many countries, partly because those who left the workforce when COVID-19 hit have not all returned.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And companies had to pay higher wages to attract workers, adding to inflationary momentum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, as many have observed, 2022 was a year of brutal inflation worldwide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Inflation reached historic levels in many advanced economies – in the United States (US), consumer prices were the highest in four decades; in Germany, they were the highest in nearly half a century.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore, too, had to contend with these inflationary pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) tightened our monetary policy five times since October 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We were able to fund these support packages from stronger-than-expected revenues, especially from corporate income tax and asset-related taxes in FY2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This additional revenue will also help to cover higher spending in other areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, the Housing and Development Board (HDB) has ramped up its Build-To-Order (BTO) supply to catch up with the backlog that had arisen from the COVID-19 delays.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means building more flats at a time when construction and land costs have increased, which in turn, requires more funding resources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In FY2022, we also drew on Past Reserves to fund our emergency COVID-19 public health expenditures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The President had earlier concurred with a draw of up to $6 billion from Past Reserves specifically for this purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is lower than the initial draw of $52 billion that the Government had sought the President's agreement for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It reflects our prudent approach in using our Reserves – drawing on them judiciously, only when there are compelling reasons to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, all in all, putting together our revenue upside with our higher spending, we expect a slight deficit of $2 billion, or 0.3% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), for FY2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We last drew on Past Reserves during the Global Financial Crisis in 2008.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We spent $4 billion in FY2009 and were able to put back what we drew two years later, due to the sharp recovery in the economy and in our fiscal position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This time, we are in a different position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economy has recovered back to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we continue to be in a tight fiscal position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is, therefore, highly unlikely that we will be able to put back what we have drawn from Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will not waver from our commitment to safeguard our Reserves as a key strategic asset.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have helped Singapore to weather major global shocks, prevent high unemployment rates and build up our capabilities, even in the midst of economic downturns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other governments spent more during this pandemic too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they largely financed their additional spending by borrowing, which will eventually have to be repaid by future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In contrast, our Reserves allowed Singapore to respond quickly without falling into debt, or burdening, either current or future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will continue to uphold our practice of fiscal prudence and the principles that underpin the protection of our Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is why it was necessary to raise the goods and services tax (GST) rate – to ensure we have the resources to take good care of our seniors and to keep a balanced Budget over the medium term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For 2023, the key factor that will shape our growth is the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, the picture is mixed and uneven, because while there are weaknesses in many parts of the world, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and other economists do not expect a global recession this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The European Union (EU) is amongst the hardest hit, due to the economic consequences of its exposure to the war in Ukraine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The US is seeing slower growth and may enter a recession, as the Federal Reserve continues to raise interest rates to combat elevated inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even so, many economists expect any contraction to be mild.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Asia is expected to continue growing this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, the COVID-19 infection wave in China has probably peaked.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As China's COVID-19 situation stabilises and it continues to reopen its economy, the pick-up in demand should provide a boost to the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our handling of the pandemic over the past three years has enhanced our reputation as a reliable and trusted node in global supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our deep relationships with both the US and China, as well as our partners in ASEAN and the wider region, make us a neutral and increasingly important place for global and regional businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will take full advantage of these opportunities to attract new flows of investments, capital, talent and ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these will add vibrancy to our economy and create more good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are major uncertainties and downside risks to this year's forecast.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A greater-than-expected decline in the US and EU economies could tip the world into recession.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may see an escalation of the Ukraine war, or a prolonged conflict and stalemate, leading to new waves of disruptions that further weigh on global trade, as well as consumer and business confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also cannot rule out a new COVID-19 variant that could be more dangerous and virulent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Whether or when these events will happen cannot be predicted with certainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must prepare ourselves for these risks and be ready to respond to them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, develop drawer plans so that we have the ability and resources to take swift action should these downside scenarios materialise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Inflation is the other major uncertainty in the global economy and a major concern for the world, and for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are some early signs that global headline inflation rates are softening.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: China's reopening will mean more demand for commodities, especially oil and gas, pushing up prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this will come at a time when Europe is still trying to secure more energy supplies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are also signs of more persistent underlying inflationary pressures, especially with tight labour markets around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We, therefore, have to brace ourselves for a period of relatively higher inflation, both globally and also in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot say how long this will last, but we expect Singapore's headline inflation to remain high, at least for the first half of this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will, therefore, do more to help Singaporeans through this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes the 70% Government risk-share for trade loans, the enhanced maximum quantum for trade and working capital loans, and support for domestic construction projects via project loans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will provide continued support for businesses in the food services, food manufacturing and retail sectors to invest in energy efficiency, and thereby, reduce the impact of higher electricity prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also help Singaporeans tide through this period of higher inflation and cushion the impact of the new GST rates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are two prongs to the support we provide to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One is the permanent GST Voucher, or GSTV scheme, which helps to permanently defray GST expenses for lower- to middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The second is the Assurance Package (AP), which provides transitional support to all Singaporeans to defray the impact of the higher GST rate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In last year's Budget, I enhanced the permanent GSTV scheme and increased the number of Singaporeans who benefit from it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will further enhance the permanent GSTV scheme, so that it continues to meaningfully defray GST expenses for eligible households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These enhancements to the permanent GSTV scheme ensure that most retirees, as well as lower-income households will not be impacted by the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I have emphasised previously, under our GST system – which means the GST and the GSTV combined – the more well-off consumers, as well as foreigners and tourists, will bear higher effective GST rates than lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This ensures that those with greater means contribute their fair share of taxes, and will effectively lower the burden of taxes on lower- and middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On top of the GSTV, we have the AP, to cushion the impact of the GST rate increase on Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In November last year, I announced that I would review and update the Package to account for higher inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, all Singaporean households can look forward to another $300 of CDC vouchers in January next year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These enhancements to the AP will enable us to maintain the commitments we had set out earlier, which is to offset additional GST expenses for at least five years for the majority of Singaporean households, and for about 10 years for the lower-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I recognise that many Singaporeans are still concerned about the immediate cost-of-living issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will provide additional support for seniors and extend a Cost-of-Living Seniors' Bonus of between $200 and $300 for eligible Singaporeans aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also double the U-Save Rebates provided to households over the next three tranches of disbursement this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In total, eligible households can expect to receive up to $760 in U-Save Rebates this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the enhancements to the GSTV scheme and AP, I would have provided comprehensive help for the majority of Singaporean households this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On average, for lower-income households, the enhancements will fully cover the increases in spending due to inflation and the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For middle-income households, the enhancements will substantially cover their increases in spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A lower-income family with two young children will receive about $5,500 in benefits this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes cash, Government top-ups to the CDA for their children, MediSave top-ups, USave and Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebates and CDC Vouchers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Help will also be extended to middle-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we have ensured that larger households, particularly those with seniors and children staying together, will receive more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, a six-person middle-income household with two seniors and two school-going children will receive about $8,400 in benefits this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The full details of the enhancements to the GSTV scheme and AP are in the Annex to this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The updates to the AP reflect the commitment of this Government to help Singaporeans through this challenging period of higher prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We provided comprehensive support last year, and we are doing so again this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I hope all Singaporeans understand that it is not fiscally sustainable to rely so heavily on Government support year after year, to cope with inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The reality is that even after the current inflation surge moderates, inflation may stabilise at a higher trend level globally, and in Singapore, higher than what we were used to in the last few decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The era of untrammelled globalisation that kept goods at highly competitive prices all over the world is over.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Countries are now relooking and adjusting their supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead of buying from the cheapest, they are prepared to accept lower efficiency and higher costs to prioritise diversification and strategic resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These trends are pushing up inflation everywhere, including Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not have much influence over this global inflation picture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But our best strategy to cope with inflation is to make ourselves more productive and competitive – so that workers earn more, and the increase in earnings can more than make up for the higher prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, this was what happened last year – real incomes grew by 2.0% for the median worker and by a higher 4.7% for a worker in the 20th percentile.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, despite higher prices, we are still better off in real terms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must, therefore, press on with economic restructuring and transformation, help businesses raise their productivity and help workers upgrade their skills at every opportunity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Great power contestation has intensified, most notably between the US and China.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the last three decades since the end of the Cold War, the world has benefited from global economic integration.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Multinational Enterprises, or MNEs, developed their supply chains based on the most cost-efficient configurations around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But now, businesses are reorganising themselves to account for once-unimaginable tail risks, including geopolitical risks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More and more MNEs are looking to reshore, onshore, or nearshore – that is, relocating factories and offices to places where they are less likely to get caught up in geostrategic crossfires.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Governments in the developed world are also embracing more muscular industrial policies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite their macroeconomic policies being generally accommodative over the past decade, growth in many of these advanced economies has been sluggish.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Incomes of middle-earners have stagnated and unemployment rates are high.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are, therefore, looking for ways to rebuild their manufacturing capabilities and create jobs for their people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this is setting off a dangerous dynamic towards greater economic nationalism and protectionism around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Governments are stumping out more aggressive support, in the form of tax breaks and subsidies, to anchor "strategic" industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The major powers increasingly view economic matters through the lens of national security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sanctions, investment prohibitions and export controls are just some of the tools that they are using to safeguard national security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, we must expect to see greater contestation and fragmentation in the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We, therefore, cannot assume that we can continue to be successful by doing the same things as we have in the past.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will need to adjust to this new era, reposition our economy and refresh our social compact for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not the first time that we have had to adapt to changes in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it will certainly not be the last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have done it many times before, through many crises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each time, we emerged with a stronger economy and a more united people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I am confident we will do it again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The key to our success is the trust we have in one another, and our solidarity and unity as a nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This year marks the 100th anniversary of the birth of Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I remember reading what he had said in 1967, soon after the turbulent period of Singapore's Independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He said, and I quote: "There is tranquillity, poise and confidence in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it is a confidence born out of the knowledge that there are very few problems which we cannot overcome…   our people's natural industry and talent will continue to blossom and flourish and generate prosperity for all." Indeed, there are very few problems we cannot overcome when we apply ourselves as one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is up to us to overcome the problems we face, to improve on what we have today and to build the Singapore we want for tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why I am glad that many Singaporeans have stepped forward to join us in the Forward Singapore exercise, sharing with us their aspirations and concerns, and joining hands and hearts to create our new social compact together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our engagements so far have affirmed the shared purpose and values that underpin our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We aspire to be a fairer and more inclusive society, and a kinder and more gracious Singapore – one where we value one another for who we are, share the responsibility of supporting each other and uphold our sense of identity in a harmonious, multiracial and multi-religious nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To achieve these shared aspirations, the Government is pursuing new strategies in a few key areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How we can continue to uplift the wages of those at the lower end of the income distribution and sustain real income growth for workers in the broad middle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How we can support workers, especially those who are displaced, with a better system of reskilling and upskilling, so that they can be retrained and placed into new jobs, and bounce back from setbacks in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How we can give everyone opportunities throughout their lives to uplift themselves, so that the circumstances of birth will not determine how far they go, and we can keep social mobility alive and well in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And how we can better look after our growing number of seniors – not just their medical and retirement needs, but also their care and living arrangements, so that they can age in place with grace, dignity and security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just a matter of having the Government do more to provide greater assurance and support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will make changes and intervene boldly where there is a need to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But Government actions must reinforce the values of personal effort, responsibility for the family and mutual support in the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are values that keep our society strong and enable our people to stand with pride and contribute to society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we must ensure that any additional spending can be funded and sustained well into the future, so that we do what is right not just for today, but also for future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That said, there are several pressing issues that have emerged in our conversations, which we will address in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that long wait times for new flats and rising resale home prices are key concerns for many young Singaporeans – we had a long discussion and debate about this in Parliament last week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also want to help parents better balance their work and family commitments, and look after their children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will move sooner on specific measures to support young, married couples and create a more conducive environment for families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Budget this year is, therefore, part of a broader exercise to chart our new way forward together and it is centred on three key thrusts to secure our future in a new era.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will grow our economy, equip our workers and provide a fuller range of opportunities for everyone to advance in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will strengthen our social compact and provide better support for families, seniors and vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will build up our collective resilience, so that we are able to bounce back strengthened from external shocks and setbacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore will have to adapt quickly to these changes, to survive and prosper in a troubled world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, redouble our efforts to attract high-quality investments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will focus on growth sectors where we can be highly competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we are a leading international financial centre in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are a global trading hub with strengths in transportation and logistics, anchored by our air and sea ports.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have a vibrant manufacturing sector, supported by key segments like electronics, chemicals and biomedical science.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These attributes and strengths will enable us to attract more multinational enterprises (MNEs) to anchor their regional, or even their global operations and headquarters in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With more high-value activities and best-in-class facilities based here, we will be able to build new capabilities, develop key industries and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also create spin-offs for our local enterprises as they serve the MNEs based here, plug into global networks and, eventually, grow to become industry leaders in their own right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must expect global competition for investments to get tougher.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting initiative, or BEPS 2.0, on the horizon, we will have less scope to use tax incentives to attract new investments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, the US and other countries are rolling out vast subsidies to build up their strategic industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will not be possible for us to outbid these countries with even bigger subsidies just to get their MNEs to invest here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But neither can we afford to be complacent and simply take our competitive position for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, have to work harder to enhance our overall productivity and workforce quality to stay competitive in this new environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will use the Fund to anchor more quality investments here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes supporting companies to build new capabilities, add greater value to our domestic ecosystems and upskill our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, these efforts will lead to better paying jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides anchoring investments and deepening capabilities, we must nurture and sustain pervasive innovation across the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to push new frontiers and differentiate ourselves in quality and value.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are restructuring and raising our game, industry by industry, through the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This scheme will significantly enhance the tax deductions for five key activities in the innovation value chain: (a) R&D conducted in Singapore; (b) Registration of intellectual property, including patents, trademarks, and designs; (c) Acquisition and licensing of intellectual property rights; (d) Innovation carried out with polytechnics and Institute of Technical Education (ITE); (e) And training via courses approved by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and aligned to the Skills Framework.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The qualifying expenditure will be capped at $400,000 for each activity, except for innovation carried out with polytechnics and ITE, for which the expenditure will be capped at $50,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With these enhancements, businesses that make full use of the scheme could enjoy tax savings of nearly 70% of their investment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some firms have yet to turn profitable, or do not have sufficient profits to maximise the benefits from the tax deductions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help smaller firms defray the costs of their innovation activities, even if they pay little or no taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our companies grow, we will support them in accessing capital to scale up and be globally competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key part of this effort is to strengthen our enterprise financing ecosystem, so that promising firms can tap on a wide range of private equity and venture capital funds, as well as financing from other financial institutions based here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has also been mobilising investments in SMEs through Heliconia Capital, which deploys equity financing to SMEs and catalyses additional growth capital from the private sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has, in turn, catalysed around $2 billion of additional investments into these companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The total revenue of this portfolio of companies has more than doubled after this investment, and over half of them have developed new capabilities or expanded beyond Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also developing a healthy pipeline of enterprises with a strong track record of international success and the potential to move to the next level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One example is Mooreast, which I visited recently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The company provides specialised anchor and mooring solutions for the offshore and marine, or the O&M, sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all know what a floating rig is; we do not always see what lies under a floating rig.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But good design, engineering and manufacturing capabilities are needed to customise mooring solutions for very different seabed and offshore conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And Mooreast, a homegrown company, is now one of the top three global players in this niche area.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it also recognises the long-term challenges of the O&M industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And so, the company is now diversifying and applying its capabilities in the offshore renewable energy market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has already secured contracts to provide the anchors for offshore wind turbines in Japan and Europe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there should be many more opportunities to come, with the growing global demand for offshore wind and other renewable energy projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do more to help promising companies, like Mooreast, grow into globally leading companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Promising companies will be offered specialised capability building programmes tailored to their needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This could involve working with experts to strengthen the core leadership team, accelerate their internationalisation plans and build a strong talent pipeline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Enterprise Singapore will also support them to secure resources to execute their growth plans, and to build sustained research and innovation capabilities so they can strengthen their value proposition and stay competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The EIS, the boost to the SME Co-Investment Fund and the SGE initiative are part of a wider suite of Government measures to help nurture and develop our enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I encourage all our companies, big and small, to make full use of these measures to innovate and grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, the value we create as an economy must benefit Singaporeans in the form of wage growth and job opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is why we have invested and will continue to invest heavily in our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through SkillsFuture, we are providing strong support for both employers and individuals to invest in upskilling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will have to do more and shift our efforts into higher gear, as we enter an era of greater volatility and economic disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of the Forward Singapore exercise, we are studying several policy moves to further strengthen our SkillsFuture ecosystem and to enhance support for displaced workers and improve pathways to better jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, I will focus on ensuring that training translates into good employment outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all know that it is good to have more skills training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some lead to recognised certifications or help workers gain specialised skills that are sought after by industry, but others may not be so relevant to industry needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Workers themselves may not know what training programmes to go for or what competencies and skills they need to secure better jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Employers, especially amongst the SMEs, may also be unfamiliar with the training landscape and often struggle to fill vacancies despite available jobseeker pools.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is, therefore, a need to develop labour market intermediaries who can work with industry, training and employment facilitation partners to optimise training and job placement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will appoint and equip Jobs-Skills Integrators to do this work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Integrators can be existing institutions, but they will have new responsibilities and outcomes to deliver.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, the Jobs-Skills Integrators will have to engage enterprises to understand the manpower and skills gap in the industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will have to work with training providers to update existing training programmes or develop new ones that will close the skills gap.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will also have to work closely with employment facilitation agencies, get buy-in from industry partners and unions, and identify individuals with the right aptitude and fit for training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the Minister for Education will share more about this at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to provide additional employment support for senior workers who wish to continue working.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have made several moves in this area, for example, raising the retirement and re-employment ages, providing wage support through the Senior Employment Credit and supporting employers who offer part-time work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One example is Mr Rahmat Hamid, who is 62 this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He retired after nearly 40 years in the hotel and F&B industries, as his children were all grown up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But he soon found that he wanted to continue working and, importantly, to contribute to society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He tried out initially as a security officer, but decided he really wanted to do something to help the elderly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, he applied for a job as a cleaner at All Saints Home, which is a senior daycare facility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And when All Saints Home saw that Mr Rahmat had valuable people management skills, they offered him a role instead as a community care associate – different from what he had applied for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a much better fit for Mr Rahmat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He is now able to put his skills to good use, and he continues to learn new skills to interact with and take care of his clients.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will continue to help lower-wage workers achieve better career progression and wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We made several major moves last year: we expanded the Progressive Wage Model to more sectors and occupations, and we required companies that employ foreign workers to pay all local employees at least the Local Qualifying Salary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, these moves cover the vast majority of lower-wage workers and will help to uplift their wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To provide transitional support for businesses, I introduced the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, or PWCS, at last year's Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also do more for specific groups of workers who may need more help to secure employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know many PwDs want to work and, if given the chance, have valuable skills to offer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More details on these schemes will be shared by the Minister for Manpower at the COS, and we will review the outcomes in 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the end, financial incentives are just one way we support PwDs and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also need dedicated efforts on the ground, through organisations like SG Enable, Yellow Ribbon Singapore and their community partners, as well as close cooperation with employers to provide meaningful job opportunities for PwDs and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The moves I have outlined represent a major investment in our enterprises and people – from SMEs to large companies and workers across various life stages and different forms of employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are doing this so that our workers and businesses can be well prepared for the future, with all its uncertainties, challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I encourage employers and workers to make the most of the support that the Government is offering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Upgrade your businesses; invest in innovation and training; reskill and upskill to stay competitive and seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we will continue to achieve quality growth in an economy that works for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even as we grow our economy and equip our workers, we will also invest significant resources to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do so in three key areas: strengthening families, tackling the related issues of inequality and social mobility, and providing better care for a rapidly ageing population.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will start with families, which form the bedrock of our society and are the anchors of emotional, social and financial support for all of us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many young Singaporeans aspire to get married and have children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One such couple is Mr Prab Nathan and Ms Saraswathy Arumugam.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter and recently welcomed a new addition to their family.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As young parents, they have many exciting plans for their family, but they also have their share of concerns and stresses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in this Budget, we will step up support for young couples like them and help them realise their aspirations in a "Singapore Made for Families".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we will do more to support the housing aspirations of young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: HDB already sets aside the bulk of its BTO flat supply for first-timer families, who are given priority for their flat applications.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the first-timer category today covers a wide range of applicants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, those who already have their own homes, but have not received housing subsidies before, are also considered first-timers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More details will be provided by the Minister for National Development at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some Singaporeans are prepared to buy resale flats for their first homes, but they find the resale prices today too expensive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have implemented cooling measures to moderate demand in the resale market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The launch and completion of more BTO projects over the next few years will further ease demand and prices for resale flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Eligible first-timer families purchasing resale flats will qualify for this increased CPF Housing Grant with immediate effect.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional grant amount will be credited into their CPF account from April this year onwards.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I will do more to support parents with the costs of raising their children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government already has a generous set of measures, including the Baby Bonus Scheme, significant preschool and education subsidies, and tax benefits like the Parenthood Tax Rebate and Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some of these schemes need to be adjusted, to ensure that more support is given to those with greater needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For Singaporean children born or adopted on or after 1 January 2024, I will change the WMCR, from a percentage of the mother's earned income to a fixed dollar relief.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will take effect from the Year of Assessment 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, for Singaporean children born or adopted before 1 January 2024, there is no change to the WMCR that their eligible working mothers can claim.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this change, eligible working mothers in the future will claim the same amount of tax relief for a child in the same child order: $8,000 in tax relief for her first child, $10,000 for her second child and $12,000 each for her third and subsequent child.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Effectively, this will provide more Government support for eligible lower- to middle-income working mothers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also lapse the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Tax Relief for all taxpayers from the Year of Assessment 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is because we already have a Migrant Domestic Worker Levy concession, which provides more targeted support for families who need help caring for their dependants, including young children below 16 years old.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Eligible first- and second-born children will receive $11,000 instead of $8,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And for the third child onwards, the Baby Bonus Cash Gift will be increased from $10,000 to $13,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, the Baby Bonus Cash Gift is disbursed in five instalments over the child's first 18 months, to help defray child-raising costs during infancy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will restructure the disbursements, so that they are paid out over a longer period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Eligible parents can expect up to $9,000 in payouts in the first 18 months of a child's life, as well as $400 every six months starting from when the child is two until the child turns six-and-a-half years old.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this way, parents can receive continuous support all the way until their child enters primary school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For eligible Singaporean children born from today, I will also increase the Government contributions to the CDA, which their parents can use to directly offset preschool and healthcare expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will increase the First Step Grant from $3,000 to $5,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is automatically credited into the CDA and parents can immediately benefit from it once they open the account.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also increase the Government co-matching cap for the CDA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the Government co-matches every dollar that parents save in the CDA, up to a cap of $3,000 and $6,000 for the couple's first and second child, respectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will increase these co-matching caps by $1,000 each, to $4,000 for the first child and $7,000 for the second child.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To cater sufficient time for the required legislative and system changes, the actual enhancements to the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, CDA First Step Grant and CDA co-matching caps will be made available from early next year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The disbursements and enhancements will be made available from early next year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will notify parents when they can make the additional deposits into their child's CDA to enjoy the enhanced Government co-matching.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes I have just described apply, as I mentioned, to eligible Singaporean children born from today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some may ask, "How about those born earlier?" In fact, at the height of the pandemic, the Government had provided a one-off Baby Support Grant of $3,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, to all young married couples: whether you already have a newborn, or are expecting a baby, or plan to have a baby, we have something to help you in your parenthood journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will better support parents in managing their work and family commitments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have been encouraging employers to adopt the voluntary Tripartite Standard on FWAs and to make these arrangements more pervasive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will implement these Tripartite Guidelines by next year, which means that employers will be required to consider staff requests for such FWAs fairly and properly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also strengthen our leave provisions for parents of infants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, eligible working fathers of Singaporean children are entitled to two weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we introduced this 10 years ago, take-up rates were low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, more than half of our fathers take paternity leave.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For a start, the extra two weeks will be given on a voluntary basis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is so that employers who are ready to grant the additional leave will be reimbursed by the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is also to give more time for employers to adjust, especially taking into account the existing economic conditions and manpower and operational challenges that many employers face.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will review this over time and intend to make this mandatory in due course.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give parents more time to bond with and care for their newborn, or to settle caregiving arrangements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All parents of Singaporean children will be eligible for this additional time-off if they have worked with their employer for a continuous period of at least three months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This, too, will apply from 1 January 2024 onwards for eligible working parents with Singaporean children aged under two years old.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, these enhancements will increase parental leave for a working couple from 22 weeks to up to 26 weeks in their child's first year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope this will provide greater assurance to parents and parents-to-be as they think about starting and raising their families in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On top of broad-based support for families, we prioritise additional support for lower-income families – to help them achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility, so that they can have dignity and aspire to a good future in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our income inequality, as measured by the Gini coefficient, has been steadily declining, as a result of deliberate policy moves like the Workfare Income Supplement, PWM and Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But helping lower-wage workers get better incomes is just one part of the equation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that the issues that lower-income individuals and families face are complex and multi-faceted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We, therefore, need a family-centric approach to provide these families with holistic and comprehensive support, and help them make lasting changes in their lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, I spoke about taking such an integrated family-centric approach through ComLink.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have since rolled out ComLink as a nationwide platform to serve 14,000 families with children living in rental housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have volunteer befrienders journeying together with the ComLink families to encourage and support them in achieving their goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The befrienders work closely with officers from the Social Service Offices, or SSOs, which coordinate family interventions at the backend, such as access to programmes and schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will now take a further step to better integrate the common functions across the different programmes in Government that support lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The SSOs will deliver these functions, and bring partners together to work in tandem, coordinating and integrating all the efforts for maximum effect.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will share more at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A critical source of support for many lower-income families is delivered through our social assistance schemes like ComCare, which help families meet their basic living expenses and work towards achieving stability and self-reliance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Part of the monies that fund ComCare come from the investment income from the ComCare Endowment Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond inequality, we must also sustain social mobility across generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, we know that the first few years matter greatly in shaping a child's potential in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must do more to close the early gaps in our children's lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have made some progress through initiatives like KidSTART, which provides upstream support for pregnant mothers and young children in lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are some early indications that KidSTART children had better preschool attendance than their peers of similar socio-economic backgrounds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Parents and caregivers on the programme also said that they were better supported in their parenting journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also made significant investments in the early childhood sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Lower-income families now pay as little as $3 a month for full-day childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The preschool enrolment rate of children aged five to six years old residing in public rental flats is now comparable to the national average.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for children aged three to four years old residing in public rental flats, the preschool enrolment rate is 80%, lower than the national average of about 88%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will continue to provide additional assistance to lower-income families and reach out to them to facilitate their children's preschool enrolment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, over the next two years, we will work with Anchor Operators to create 22,000 more full-day childcare places and expand the number of Ministry of Education (MOE) Kindergartens.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help support higher preschool participation rates across the board, and especially among lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the other end of the demographic spectrum, Singapore is one of the fastest-ageing nations in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above, up from one in six today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While many are living longer, some do spend their final years in ill health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This, coupled with smaller household sizes, will mean an increased burden of care for families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nursing homes are suitable for the elderly with high-care needs and little to no family support, but we cannot rely on this as the mainstream solution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, many seniors themselves prefer to be cared for in the community and to grow old in an environment that is familiar to them, surrounded by their loved ones.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, need to review and update our approaches to aged care – to ensure seniors live as much of their lives in good health as possible and have ample options to age in the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our first line of defence is that of preventive care.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why our priority is to support seniors to take care of their own health, including by remaining physically and mentally active, and staying engaged in their communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we have introduced Healthier SG, as an empowering strategy, so that seniors can take preventive care steps together with their doctors and community partners to improve their health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will enable seniors to keep chronic illnesses at bay, or if they do contract them, to detect the diseases early, so that these can be kept under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The refreshed Action Plan for Successful Ageing, launched last month, supports Healthier SG by setting out a comprehensive set of initiatives for seniors to better care for themselves, continue contributing and stay connected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for seniors to stay active and healthy, or to better manage their existing chronic illnesses, they will need stronger support in the community, outside of hospitals and clinics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of the Forward Singapore exercise, we are studying how we can enhance the range of care and support options within the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes reviewing the operating model of Active Ageing Centres and examining how we can better strengthen and coordinate the providers in the aged care sector, which is highly fragmented today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our population ages, we will also have to address the retirement needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have enhanced the CPF system over the years, such as through Workfare and extra interest on lower CPF balances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We now have Silver Support to supplement the retirement income of seniors who had low incomes in their working years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we also encourage family members with more means to top up their loved ones' CPF through tax reliefs and matching grants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are considering what more we can do to enhance retirement adequacy in our Forward Singapore deliberations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, in this Budget, I will make several moves to help specific segments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, the Government had earlier convened the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers to look into strengthening protections for Platform Workers, including improving their housing and retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has accepted the Committee's recommendations, one of which was to align the CPF contribution rates of Platform Workers and Companies with those of employees and employers over a period of five years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Platform Companies will also be required to pay CPF contributions for these Platform Workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These changes will help Platform Workers raise their total earnings and strengthen their housing and retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in the short term, they will affect the take-home pay of these workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will, therefore, introduce additional support to help lower-income Platform Workers cushion the impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More information on this Transition Support is in the Annex and the Minister for Manpower will also share more at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also make some CPF adjustments for older workers, in line with the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We implemented the first increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2022 and the second increase earlier this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For these two increases, the Government had provided employers with a CPF Transition Offset to alleviate the increase in business cost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue with the next increase in CPF contribution rates in 2024 and, likewise, provide employers with a similar offset.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also help middle-income Singaporeans save more for their retirement by raising the CPF monthly salary ceiling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The CPF salary ceilings were last raised in 2016.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will phase in the increases over four years, starting from this year, to allow employers and employees to adjust to the changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We still have more to do and will continue this important work as part of Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a world characterised by greater uncertainties and volatility, we need to build a more resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have kept an eye on resilience throughout our nation-building journey, but we are entering a new era where disruptions will likely happen more frequently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will have to consider additional redundancies and safety buffers that we can fall back on during a crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Having such buffers does not mean that we will not suffer damage when hit by a shock, but it will enhance our ability to absorb the shock, rebound from the crisis and emerge stronger from it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we should recognise that building resilience comes at a price.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, diversification means buying from multiple sources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this also makes things more expensive, because we are no longer buying only from the cheapest source.
