speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The stockpiles of food and essential items will require space and will need to be maintained.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even if a crisis does not materialise or is less severe than expected, such costs still need to be funded.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will spend more on resilience, but we also need to be judicious in how we use public monies to secure effective and enduring improvements in our national resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One key strategy is to build strong organisational capabilities to respond quickly and effectively during crises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, learning from the experience in Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS), we set up the National Public Health Laboratory and the National Centre for Infectious Diseases.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These new capabilities proved critical in treating, managing and fighting the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During this pandemic, the outbreak in the migrant worker dormitories was a major challenge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had to draw on resources from the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), the Home Team and other Government agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is just one example of how we continue to build up organisational capabilities within the Public Service to deal with crises and emergencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are also limits to how much we can grow headcount in the Public Service, especially with slower growth in our resident labour force.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we will continue to adjust our resources and manpower – to do less in some existing areas where the needs have come down and to reallocate the funds and headcount to new priority areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During the pandemic, we also had to mobilise and cross-deploy public servants for various crisis roles, for example, to help with contact tracing or the manning of call centres.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are, therefore, looking at how we can put in place a more comprehensive system for such training and cross-deployment, based on the expertise and skillsets of our officers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the Public Service, we will need to tap on the capabilities of the private and people sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, we saw many excellent examples of such partnerships in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In healthcare, we were able to leverage the capabilities of our private hospitals and private general practitioner (GP) clinics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Outside of healthcare, our companies and non-governmental organisation (NGO) groups stepped up in many different ways – housing and taking care of migrant workers, setting up and manning the community care facilities at Changi Expo and Changi Exhibition Centre, ensuring continued access to vital supply chains and facilitating our crucial nationwide vaccine operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will learn from these experiences and put in place structures that will enable us to harness our resources more effectively and strengthen the complementary roles that the public, private and people sectors can play during peacetime and in crises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another important aspect of resilience is in our economy and supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to review our stockpiling strategies and improve the diversification of critical supplies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will weigh the costs of such insurance carefully and ensure that the benefits we reap in terms of greater resilience are worth the additional costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, we have built resilience in our infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have designed our buildings to serve both peacetime and crisis functions where possible, given our land scarcity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, our MRT stations are designed to function as public shelters and provide protection during wartime emergencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this pandemic, we had to convert, at short notice, several existing spaces – vacant schools were used to house recovering migrant workers; community centres became vaccination centres; hotels became quarantine facilities; and exhibition halls became additional healthcare facilities to augment hospital bed capacity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this reinforces the importance of having adaptable, multi-use facilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, therefore, study how we can further enhance the resilience of our infrastructure, especially for new major projects like the Tuas Mega Port and Changi Airport Terminal 5.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The lessons from COVID-19 will also help us in strengthening our resilience against the larger existential threat of global warming and climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have accelerated the low-carbon transition for Singapore to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are raising the carbon tax progressively over the next few years to provide a stronger price signal and impetus to reduce our carbon footprint.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are supporting our enterprises and households to become more energy efficient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are greening our buildings and going for cleaner vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are harvesting solar energy, transiting to cleaner energy sources, like hydrogen, and working with our neighbours to develop regional power grids.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, we are doing everything we can to fight climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we also know that our efforts alone will not be enough.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The rest of the world must also do their part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, in the short term, many countries are increasing their reliance on fossil fuels to prevent the lights from going out and to provide for energy security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This simply means the world will have to redouble its efforts to get back on track with the plans to keep global temperatures from rising beyond a threshold that will result in irreversible damage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we will do our best to shape and drive this international agenda, we must also prepare for the worst.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since then, the teams have been conducting site-specific studies for drainage enhancements and coastal protection, starting with the stretch from the city to East Coast.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We expect climate-related spending to go up significantly in the medium term, and we will commit more resources as we progressively implement these extensive infrastructure plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Be it a pandemic, an economic crisis or rising sea levels, we have been systematically planning forward, to give ourselves more options and solutions to cope with future shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will not be able to anticipate and cater for every scenario.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Furthermore, no amount of buffers or redundancies in our system can mitigate the extreme scenarios of blockades, conflict, war or climate disasters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just look at the extent of destruction and damage that has happened in Ukraine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The cost of rebuilding the country has been estimated at several hundreds of billions of dollars and that figure is only expected to grow as the war continues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, our best safeguard in any crisis remains having access to the financial reserves we have accumulated over decades of prudent government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They allow us to respond quickly to immediate needs in an emergency, without compromising the focus on the longer term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They enable us to bounce back stronger, as has happened during the Global Financial Crisis in 2008 and most recently in this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if we were ever to be hit by a bigger calamity or disaster, our Reserves will provide us the resources we need to rebuild Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Aside from financial reserves, the most critical ingredient of national resilience is our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When there is a high level of solidarity and trust amongst our citizens, and when Singaporeans feel a strong sense of collective ownership and responsibility for each other, we will be able to withstand any shocks together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we are continually reviewing and updating our policies to keep our social fabric strong and resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do so from a position of strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over decades of engagement and hard work, we have expanded the common stakes that we have in each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have kept faith with each other and avoided the fissures that have divided so many other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the last three years of the pandemic, we have seen many ground-up initiatives by diverse groups, looking after the more vulnerable amongst us, regardless of race or religion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will continue to do our part to foster this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One way is through tax deductible donations to Institutions of a Public Character, or IPCs, and eligible institutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our tax deduction for donations at 250% is, in fact, already very high, compared to other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to encourage businesses to do their part in corporate giving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The scope of eligible activities for tax incentives under this Scheme will be expanded.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will also double the qualifying per-IPC cap to $100,000 per calendar year to facilitate deeper partnerships between businesses and IPCs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our charities, social service agencies, or SSAs, and community organisations play crucial roles in looking after the vulnerable, and mobilising Singaporeans to support those in greater need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to strengthen their capabilities and support their services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have completed a review of social service sector salary benchmarks, and will work with the SSAs to raise salaries so as to better attract and retain talent in the social service sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will share more at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Community Silver Trust provides dollar-for-dollar donation matching grants for the SSAs and will enable them to enhance the quality and accessibility of community care, especially for the more vulnerable seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are doing good work on the ground, and are well placed to provide assistance to members of their respective communities who need help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are reminded that every citizen and every sector of society has a part to play in ensuring Singapore's security and defending our way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, our efforts to strengthen our overall resilience must reflect the values that motivate us as a people and as a nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want a Singapore where we not only do the best for ourselves, but also help our fellow citizens succeed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we keep Singapore strong, resilient and united.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: (In Mandarin):   This year's Budget is taking place amidst significant changes in the external environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to focus our efforts to ensure Singapore continues to survive and prosper in a troubled world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand that Singaporeans are concerned about the rising cost-of-living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, I will provide more support to help Singaporeans tide through this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Retirees and lower-income households will receive the most benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, an elderly retired couple living in a 3-room HDB flat will receive $6,500 in 2023.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, our measures will fully cover their increased expenses due to higher GST rate and inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Middle-income families will also receive help and those with more people in the household will get more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, a middle-income family of six living in a 5-room HDB flat, with two school-going children and two grandparents, will receive a total of $8,400 this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the middle-income groups, our measures will substantially cover their increased expenses due to higher GST and inflation this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides these temporary measures, I will enhance the permanent GSTV scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This ensures that most retirees as well as lower-income households will not be impacted by the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under our GST system, it is the more well-off consumers, as well as foreigners and tourists who will bear higher effective GST rates than lower-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides tackling cost of living concerns, we will equip our businesses and workers to seize the opportunities in this new era.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will support our local enterprises, especially SMEs, to invest in innovation projects and activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through innovation, we want our companies to innovate and grow their businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also do more to help promising SMEs to internationalise, expand into new markets overseas and compete on the global stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope some local companies will become globally leading enterprises and hold their own against the best in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do more to support the reskilling and upskilling of our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also strengthen our support for families to reduce the cost of raising children, especially in their early years, and help parents better manage their work and family commitments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This year marks the 100th birth anniversary of our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to steward the values underpinning Mr Lee's legacy, to plan for the long term, determine our own destiny and create the future we want, for ourselves and for the generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore has faced one challenge after another since we became independent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have prevailed in every challenge and emerged stronger year after year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has been our experience after fighting the pandemic together for the last three years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will see multiple challenges in this Year of the Rabbit, but also new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must not adopt a "wait-and-see" attitude; instead, we should be nimble like a rabbit and act decisively to embrace the opportunities ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So long as we remain united as one people, I am confident we will be able to build a better and stronger Singapore for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: (In English): Sir, our efforts to grow the economy, strengthen social safety nets, and enhance national resilience will require the Government to spend more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Ministry of Finance recently published an Occasional Paper on our medium-term fiscal projections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our expenditure projections have not taken into account additional policy moves that the Government may make in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there are any such further increases in spending, they will need to be funded by additional revenues to ensure a balanced Budget for the medium term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But even if we have to look at ways to raise revenues in future, the Government will keep our overall system of taxes and benefits fair and progressive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every citizen has a part to play in nation building.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Everyone contributes something, but those who are better off contribute more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, everyone benefits from the State's spending, with the vulnerable benefiting more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, besides the GST rate increase, I made major changes to strengthen our tax structure, including raising the Personal Income Tax rates for top income-earners, as well as the property tax rates for higher-value owner-occupied residential properties and all non-owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This year, I will make further adjustments to our tax system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will adjust the Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) regime which applies to all purchases or receipt of gifts of immovable properties in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will introduce higher marginal BSD rates for higher-value residential and non-residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional conveyance duties regime will also be adjusted accordingly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These changes are expected to affect 60% of non-residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the actual amount will depend on the state of the property market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I had adjusted vehicle taxes last year, but there is still scope to make them more progressive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will therefore adjust the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) rates to better differentiate between the higher end cars and also tax luxury cars at a higher rate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, the Preferential ARF rebates are sized as a percentage of the payable ARF.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will cap the Preferential ARF rebates at $60,000 to avoid providing excessive rebates to more expensive cars when they are deregistered.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These changes are expected to affect the top one-third of cars by OMV.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Buyers of cars with an OMV of $40,000 or less will not be affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The new ARF structure and the Preferential ARF cap will apply to all cars registered with COEs obtained from the next round of COE bidding.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The ARF change is expected to generate about $200 million in additional revenue per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But again, the actual amount will depend on the state of the vehicle market  .

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To discourage the consumption of tobacco products, I will implement a 15% increase in tobacco excise duty across all tobacco products, with effect from today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The increase is expected to generate about $100 million in additional revenue per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also make some tax adjustments to support businesses and strengthen our competitiveness, as well as to enhance the fairness and resilience of our tax system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The details of these tax changes are in the Annex to the Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our corporate tax system will be affected by BEPS 2.0.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, many jurisdictions have not announced their implementation plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some key parameters of Pillar Two have only been finalised this year, while others remain under discussion at the international level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The EU recently announced its plans to implement Pillar Two in phases starting effectively from 2024.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other jurisdictions like the United Kingdom (UK) and Switzerland have announced their intention to do the same.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As the rules will be implemented progressively, the full effects will only be felt in 2025 or later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will review and update our broader suite of industry development schemes to ensure that Singapore remains competitive in attracting and retaining investments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That said, the developments on BEPS 2.0 are fluid, and we will continue to monitor international developments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there are additional delays, we will adjust our implementation timelines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to engage companies and give them sufficient notice, well ahead of any changes to our tax rules or schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For FY2022, as I mentioned just now, I expect an overall deficit of $2 billion, or 0.3% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is appropriate for the projected economic conditions this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nonetheless, we will have drawer plans in place to take swift action, should downside economic scenarios materialise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the last three financial years, we have had to draw on the Past Reserves to cope with the unexpected shocks and disruptions of the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As things return to normal, we will not need to make any draw on the Past Reserves in this year's Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In May 2020, the Government raised the Contingencies Funds balance from $3 billion to $16 billion, to ensure we could respond quickly to urgent and unforeseen cashflow needs arising from the fast-evolving pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will ensure adequate resources for unforeseen circumstances, while retaining discipline in how we manage our finances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we can increase the balances in the Contingencies Funds, but there is no legal mechanism to make a reduction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will, hence, amend the Constitution for this purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will be tabling a Bill for its First Reading later this month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are taking comprehensive measures to help Singaporeans tide through the immediate cost-of-living pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, we are making decisive moves to secure Singapore's prospects – by growing our economy, equipping our workers, strengthening our social compact and building a more resilient nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These moves are part of the broader strategy for our next bound of development, which we are co-creating with Singaporeans through the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it has never been and will never be that easy for us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are a little red dot – a country that was never meant to be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are more exposed and vulnerable than others to external forces beyond our control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And in our short history since Independence, we have repeatedly faced crises and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have never shied away from adversity and challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew and our Pioneer Generation set the tone for how we should respond – with grit and tenacity, and with the courage to dream big and to turn these dreams into reality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And since then, successive generations have sustained the hard work to take Singapore forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we are in a much stronger position today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also emerged from the last three years of COVID-19 more united than before.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a high regard around the world for the Singapore brand – our honesty, integrity and reliability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Investors trust us – they see advantage in our tripartite system, our open economy and our cohesive society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are fundamentals that will continue to set us apart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But our real strength is in our people – who we are and what we stand for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are a people with an indomitable and "never-say-die" spirit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are quick in adapting and responding to changes in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We believe in stretching ourselves, pursuing excellence and striving to do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we strive, not just for ourselves and our families, but also for those around us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because we are also a caring, gracious and generous people – we treat each other as equals, we respect and look out for one another, and we are ever ready to extend a helping hand to those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We see this spirit in Singaporeans like Ms Emily Yap, who is a registered nurse at Alexandra Hospital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Emily has been hard at work at the COVID-19 frontlines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite this heavy workload, she still volunteers on her off-days to care for the wider community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She draws inspiration from her grandmother, who also worked as a nurse her whole life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, Emily started a ground-up initiative with other like-minded young people.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the Financial Year 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
